title: Buddy Bolden's band and its trombonists
summary: He heard Bolden and Robichaux at Lincoln Park; Bolden's trombonist was Ed Jones, with Carnish, and Frankie Dusen asked about.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you ever hear Buddy Bolden's band? Do you remember?
Yes sir. I remember Buddy Bolden being good. Him and John Robeshow, at that time it was just them two bands, I believe, bucking at each other. Most of it I knew of. He worked very good.
Where did you hear Bolden? Was he up in Jefferson or down here?
Heard him in Jefferson, heard him down here. See? Heard him down there. Yeah Lincoln Park. Heard him down there. Yeah Lincoln Park. Robeshow played. And there were many places where they both played.
Who was his trombone player in Bolden, do you know? When you heard them?
Let me see. I believe he had a vowel trombone player by the name of Ed Jones.
Yeah he was good. Good vowel trombone player. You know he played. Plenty Headway and Boyle at Plenty Headway.
I don't know him. Somebody told me once that Carnish had played with him. Do you remember Carnish? Carnish, yeah I know him good.

You knew him? He played with Boyle too. I think Ed Jones was the first. Well between him and Carnish, I know where Carnish played with him. And I know Ed Jones played with him. And the both was good. Yeah, Carnish played with him.
Did Frankie Doosen ever play with Bolden? Do you remember?

Not as I know of. No, I don't know. I don't think Frankie Doosen would play with Bolden. Maybe he was. He could have played with him, but I don't remember him. But he was a good old trombone player too. He had plenty headway with him. Not much of a year. Plenty headway.
